title: What a Name Means: Namespaces, Private Names and Remapping

questions.question: Two robots each run a lidar driver that publishes scan. What puts them on different topics?
options: Each node's name is resolved against its own namespace: /robot1/scan and /robot2/scan, apart, while an absolute /scan would be the same for both
questions.explanation: The name in the node is not the name on the bus.

questions.question: For node lidar_driver in /robot1, what does ~/status mean?
options: /robot1/lidar_driver/status: a private name goes inside a namespace named for the node
questions.explanation: A private name is where the node puts what is its own.

questions.question: Which of these is not a valid topic name?
options: a//b, which has an empty part, and so do names with a trailing slash, a space, or a part starting with a digit
questions.explanation: The test rejected all 16 bad names and accepted all 9 good ones.

questions.question: What is wrong with a node that publishes to /scan?
options: The name is absolute and ignores the namespace, so two robots share one topic with two publishers
questions.explanation: Write relative names in a node and leave absolute ones for things that are truly global.

questions.question: What does a remap rule apply to?
options: The resolved name: the same rule in a node in /robot2 is about /robot2/scan and does not apply to /robot1/scan
questions.explanation: A rule is read the same way as any name.

questions.question: What does the root namespace contribute to a name?
options: Nothing, so scan in the root is /scan and not //scan
questions.explanation: The namespace is made to look the same however it was written.
